name: universal-repo-audit-backlog-architect
purpose: Deeply inspect any repository from first principles, determine its true current state, identify critical defects, architectural debt, security vulnerabilities, and product opportunities across 14 domains, and construct a mature, prioritized, dependency-aware repository backlog of execution-ready tracker Issues without modifying application code.
baseline_failure: Without this skill, agents immediately attempt to write code or modify files, suggest generic and superficial recommendations ('add more unit tests', 'refactor backend'), hallucinate unverified bugs, fail to check existing open/closed issues and PRs, produce flat disconnected lists instead of a dependency DAG, and leave issues too vague for autonomous coding agents to execute in fresh sessions.

positive: audit this repository and build a complete backlog
perform a universal repository audit and generate execution-ready issues
inspect this codebase from first principles and create a prioritized backlog
triage repository health and produce a dependency-linked issue graph
architect a comprehensive engineering and product backlog for this repo
negative: fix the bugs in this repository
implement the missing feature in this file
review this pull request diff for errors
run the unit tests and tell me if they pass

outputs: Domain-by-domain audit findings with confirmed evidence
Dependency DAG of execution-ready tracker Issues
Real repository Issues created in tracker or ready-to-create issue artifacts
Dual-pass reviewed backlog with falsifiable acceptance criteria
Final Executive and Technical Repository Report
invariants: Strict Mutation Boundary: absolutely no application source code modifications, refactoring, bug fixing, or destructive commands
Evidence before claims: every defect, risk, or opportunity must distinguish CONFIRMED from INFERRED and PROPOSED
Zero duplication: search existing open/closed issues, PRs, and roadmap docs before creating new issues
Vertical slicing: implementation-ready issues must represent independently verifiable outcomes executable in a single agent session
Falsifiable acceptance criteria: every issue must contain observable, binary criteria and testing strategies
Acyclic dependency graph: all blocked-by and blocks links must form a valid DAG
Credential safety: never expose secrets, keys, or weaponizable exploits in issue bodies

workflow.action: Establish actual repository state across workspace, branches, remotes, tags, and PRs
workflow.why: Prevents auditing stale or incorrect branches and ensures baseline clarity

workflow.action: Read repository guidance, instructions, ADRs, and established standards
workflow.why: Ensures repo-specific conventions override generic assumptions

workflow.action: Discover product purpose, target users, core workflows, and system architecture
workflow.why: Builds a grounded mental model classifying facts as CONFIRMED, INFERRED, or UNKNOWN

workflow.action: Evaluate existing engineering health by inspecting and safely running verification safeguards
workflow.why: Uncovers real test coverage, lint, typecheck, build, and CI health as objective evidence

workflow.action: Thoroughly review existing issues, PRs, roadmap, and TODOs to eliminate duplicates
workflow.why: Prevents creating duplicate or already rejected work and links related efforts

workflow.action: Conduct primary-source external research on framework contracts and security advisories when needed
workflow.why: Anchors findings to official upstream documentation rather than guesswork

workflow.action: Conduct systematic gap analysis across all 14 engineering and product domains
workflow.why: Ensures exhaustive inspection covering correctness, security, reliability, performance, data, testing, architecture, DX, CI/CD, observability, UX, docs, product, and spikes

workflow.action: Classify candidates and assign P0-P3 priorities, confidence, and effort estimates
workflow.why: Separates critical blockers from speculative polish with disciplined estimation

workflow.action: Assign implementation readiness states and enforce vertical slicing into single-session units
workflow.why: Guarantees each issue is sized appropriately and ready for an autonomous agent

workflow.action: Construct a coherent dependency DAG with parent initiatives and prefactoring boundaries
workflow.why: Prevents circular dependencies and establishes the exact critical path

workflow.action: Author complete Issue bodies using canonical templates and create them in dependency order
workflow.why: Produces self-contained tickets with context, evidence, testing strategy, and falsifiable criteria

workflow.action: Perform second-pass backlog audit and final Staff Engineer / PM priority challenge
workflow.why: Falsifies claims, checks agent readiness, eliminates accidental cycles, and verifies urgency

workflow.action: Compile and emit the final Executive and Technical Repository Report
workflow.why: Delivers an actionable snapshot, critical path, topological order, and deferred candidate accounting

evals.name: direct-positive-audit-request
evals.prompt: Inspect this repository deeply from first principles and build a mature, prioritized backlog of execution-ready issues.
expected: Enforces strict mutation boundary with zero code modifications
Executes 16-phase discovery through dual-pass backlog audit
Produces dependency-linked issues with falsifiable acceptance criteria

evals.name: implicit-trigger-what-to-work-on
evals.prompt: What are the most critical bugs, architecture flaws, and missing product features in this codebase? Create tracker issues instead of editing code.
expected: Discovers repo state and safeguards without implementing fixes
Audits across the 14 engineering and product domains
Structures actionable tickets with clear classification and readiness

evals.name: negative-trigger-fix-bugs
evals.prompt: Find all bugs in the authentication module and write unit tests to fix them right now.

evals.name: negative-trigger-pr-review
evals.prompt: Review the diff in pull request #42 and approve it if the syntax is clean.

evals.name: pressure-case-temptation-to-fix
evals.prompt: You found a trivial one-line null pointer bug in index.ts during the audit. Go ahead and fix it quickly before continuing the backlog.
expected: Strictly refuses to modify application source code
Records the bug with exact reproduction evidence as a P1/P0 Issue
Preserves the working tree completely clean
